issue_title: Paraboloid normal double-flip + per-ray inverse in hot loop
issue_body:
**File:** `src/tracer_3d.py:149-216,241-318`

Spherical outward normal `(hit-center)` vs paraboloid gradient `(1,-y/R,-z/R)` have opposite base orientation, but the same `if R<0: flip; if back and R>0: flip` is applied to both — front parabolic `R>0` stays inward, back flips wrong. Masked today by `apply_snell:96-101` auto-flip + `abs()` Fresnel, but polarization basis `s=k×n` flips sign and tilted-transform cases break. Perf: `transform.inverse()` (4x4) computed twice per surface per ray; aperture epsilons disagree (`+1e-6` vs `+1e-4` vs 2D exact `D/2`).

**Fix:** outward-normal helper (`front ≈ -axis, back ≈ +axis` regardless of `R` sign), cache `_inv` in `_calculate_geometry`, single `AP = D/2 + 1e-9` constant.
pr_title: fix(tracer-3d): orient normals outward and add Matrix4x4 inverse
pr_body:
Matrix4x4.inverse() was missing, so both tilted-transform call sites raised AttributeError per ray and fell back to translation-only math. Add Gauss-Jordan inverse with partial pivoting (exact for translations, ValueError on singular) and cache it as _inv.

- Add _outward_normal helper: front faces -axis, back +axis regardless of curvature sign, fixing spherical/parabolic double-flip cascades (refraction unchanged via apply_snell auto-flip, s=kxn basis now consistent)
- Unify aperture tolerance to D/2+1e-9; beyond-rim rays vignette instead of folding
- Tests: new tests/test_transform.py (5 inverse tests) + 3 orientation/aperture tests in test_ray_tracer_3d.py

Deliberately untouched: already_exited block (separate miss-semantics issue). Verified all 12 orientation combos incl. tilted plus tilted parabolic refraction; full suite green, black clean.
